words.definition: a biological catalyst, usually a protein, that speeds up a specific chemical reaction without being consumed
words.example: Enzymes increase reaction rates by lowering activation energy.

words.definition: a substance produced by living organisms that increases the rate of a biochemical reaction without being used up
words.example: Most biological catalysts are enzymes.

words.definition: the total set of chemical reactions occurring in a cell or organism
words.example: Metabolism includes both building and breakdown reactions.

words.definition: metabolic reactions that build larger molecules from smaller ones and require energy
words.example: Protein synthesis is an example of anabolism.

words.definition: metabolic reactions that break larger molecules into smaller ones and release usable energy
words.example: Cell respiration includes catabolic reactions.

words.definition: the region of an enzyme where a specific substrate binds and the reaction is catalysed
words.example: The shape and chemistry of an active site determine which substrates can bind.

words.definition: a reactant molecule on which an enzyme acts
words.example: Amylase binds starch as its substrate.

words.definition: the temporary association formed when a substrate binds to an enzyme's active site
words.example: An enzyme-substrate complex forms before products are released.

words.definition: the tendency of an enzyme to bind and catalyse only one substrate or a narrow range of substrates
words.example: Enzyme specificity depends on interactions at the active site.

words.definition: the minimum energy required for reactants to reach a state from which a reaction can proceed
words.example: Enzymes lower the activation energy of biochemical reactions.

words.definition: the temperature at which an enzyme-catalysed reaction proceeds at its maximum rate under given conditions
words.example: Human enzymes often have optimum temperatures near normal body temperature.

words.definition: the pH at which an enzyme-catalysed reaction has its highest rate
words.example: Pepsin has an acidic optimum pH.

words.definition: the amount of substrate present per unit volume
words.example: Increasing substrate concentration raises enzyme activity until active sites become saturated.

words.definition: the amount of enzyme present per unit volume
words.example: Increasing enzyme concentration can increase reaction rate when substrate is abundant.

words.definition: an enzyme whose three-dimensional shape has been disrupted so that normal catalytic function is reduced or lost
words.example: An enzyme may become denatured at high temperature.

words.definition: the change in amount or concentration of reactant or product per unit time
words.example: The rate of reaction can be measured by tracking product formation.

words.definition: the controlled release of energy from organic compounds to produce ATP
words.example: Cell respiration transfers chemical energy from glucose into ATP.

words.definition: ATP, a nucleotide with three phosphate groups that transfers usable energy in cells
words.example: Adenosine triphosphate powers many cellular processes.

words.definition: adenosine diphosphate, a nucleotide that can be phosphorylated to form ATP
words.example: ADP combines with inorganic phosphate when ATP is regenerated.

words.definition: an inorganic phosphate group that can be added to ADP to form ATP
words.example: Energy is used to attach phosphate to ADP.

words.definition: movement or conversion of energy from one form, molecule or process to another
words.example: ATP enables energy transfer between catabolic and energy-requiring processes.

words.definition: cell respiration that uses oxygen and releases large amounts of energy from organic substrates
words.example: Aerobic respiration of glucose produces carbon dioxide and water.

words.definition: energy-releasing respiration that occurs without oxygen
words.example: Some organisms use anaerobic respiration when oxygen is unavailable.

words.definition: an organic molecule that can be broken down in respiration to release energy
words.example: Glucose is a common respiratory substrate.

words.definition: a gas used as the final electron acceptor in aerobic respiration
words.example: Oxygen uptake increases when aerobic respiration rate rises.

words.definition: a gaseous product released during oxidation of carbon-containing respiratory substrates
words.example: Carbon dioxide is produced during aerobic respiration of glucose.

words.definition: a product of aerobic respiration formed when oxygen is reduced
words.example: Water is formed during the final stages of aerobic respiration.

words.definition: aerobic ATP-producing reactions that occur in mitochondria of eukaryotic cells
words.japanese: ミトコンドリアでの好気呼吸
words.example: Mitochondrial aerobic respiration supplies most ATP in many active eukaryotic cells.

words.definition: the rate at which an organism or tissue carries out cellular respiration
words.example: Respiration rate can be estimated from oxygen consumption.

words.definition: an apparatus used to measure gas exchange associated with respiration, commonly oxygen uptake
words.example: A respirometer can compare respiration rates at different temperatures.

words.definition: the removal or consumption of oxygen by an organism, tissue or cell
words.example: Oxygen uptake by germinating seeds reflects aerobic respiration.

words.definition: a cellular activity that needs an input of usable energy, often supplied by ATP
words.japanese: エネルギーを必要とする過程
words.example: Active transport is an energy-requiring process.

words.definition: the process by which light energy is used to synthesize organic compounds from carbon dioxide and water
words.example: Photosynthesis converts light energy into chemical energy stored in organic molecules.

words.definition: a molecule that absorbs particular wavelengths of light used in photosynthesis
words.example: Chlorophyll is the main photosynthetic pigment in green plants.

words.definition: a green photosynthetic pigment that absorbs light energy
words.japanese: クロロフィル・葉緑素
words.example: Chlorophyll absorbs strongly in blue and red regions of visible light.

words.definition: a graph showing how strongly a pigment absorbs different wavelengths of light
words.example: The absorption spectrum of chlorophyll has peaks in blue and red light.

words.definition: a graph showing the effectiveness of different wavelengths in driving a biological process such as photosynthesis
words.example: The photosynthesis action spectrum broadly matches chlorophyll absorption.

words.definition: a technique that separates components of a mixture according to differences in movement between phases
words.example: Paper chromatography can separate pigments extracted from leaves.

words.definition: the ratio of the distance travelled by a solute to the distance travelled by the solvent front in chromatography
words.example: An Rf value can help identify a pigment after chromatography.

words.definition: photosynthetic reactions that require light energy to generate energy-rich products and release oxygen
words.example: The light-dependent reactions occur in thylakoid membranes.

words.definition: photosynthetic reactions that use products of the light-dependent stage to fix carbon dioxide into organic compounds
words.example: The light-independent reactions build carbohydrates from fixed carbon.

words.definition: the amount of light energy reaching a surface per unit area and time
words.example: At low levels, increasing light intensity can increase photosynthesis rate.

words.definition: the amount of carbon dioxide present in a given volume
words.example: Low carbon dioxide concentration can limit photosynthesis.

words.definition: restriction of a biological process because temperature is below or above the range for maximum activity
words.example: Low temperature can limit photosynthesis by slowing enzyme-controlled reactions.

words.definition: an environmental variable in shortest effective supply that restricts the rate of photosynthesis
words.example: Light can be the photosynthetic limiting factor on a dark day.

words.definition: the amount of photosynthetic activity per unit time
words.example: Oxygen production can be used as an indicator of photosynthesis rate.

words.definition: release of molecular oxygen during photosynthesis
words.example: Aquatic plants release bubbles of oxygen during photosynthesis.

words.definition: an experimental method using floating leaf disks to estimate photosynthesis rate
words.example: In a leaf disk assay, faster floating can indicate faster oxygen accumulation.
